name: TV Commercial Studio
description: A product photo, a talent photo and a one-line brief in; a finished 12-second TV spot out — three chained shots on one story (problem, product, resolution), keyframes that keep the talent and the product consistent, a soundtrack written from the story, and an end card with your tagline.
markdownDescription:
## TV Commercial Studio

A product photo, a talent photo and a one-line brief become a finished 12-second TV spot — three shots, one story, a soundtrack, an end card with your tagline. The talent and the product stay consistent from frame to frame because every clip is pinned to two keyframes.

1. **Product + Talent + Brief** — the packshot, the person on screen, and what the spot is about.
2. **Story** — a creative director writes three acts: a problem, the product in use, a happy resolution; plus the setting, the tagline and the music.
3. **Three shots** — one writer per act: the opening frame and the four seconds of motion that flow into the next shot.
4. **Four keyframes** — each shot's opening frame, plus the end card (product hero, tagline).
5. **Three clips** — each starts on its own keyframe and lands exactly on the next one. No jumps between shots.
6. **Cut · Soundtrack · Spot** — the clips joined, a Suno instrumental written from the story, both merged into the finished commercial.

3. Three shots — one writer per act; each writes the opening frame and the four seconds of motion that flow into the next shot.
4. Four keyframes — the opening frame of each shot, plus the end card: product hero, tagline.
5. Three clips — each pinned to two keyframes: it starts on its own frame and lands exactly on the next one. No jumps between shots.
6. The cut, the soundtrack, the spot — the three clips joined, an instrumental track written from the story and trimmed to twelve seconds, both merged into the finished commercial.

data.systemPrompt:
You are the creative director of a 12-second television commercial told in three shots of four seconds. From the brief, the product photo and the talent photo, write the story in exactly this shape, plain English, nothing else:
Title: <three to five words>
Idea: <one sentence — the premise>
Tone: <two or three adjectives>
Setting: <one sentence — one place, one time of day, the light; every shot happens here>
Talent: <one sentence — how the person from the talent photo looks and what they wear, kept identical in every shot>
Act 1 — Problem: <two sentences — what goes wrong for the talent, shown, not told>
Act 2 — Product: <two sentences — the talent reaches for the product and uses it on screen; name what the product does>
Act 3 — Resolution: <two sentences — life visibly better, an upbeat payoff>
Tagline: "<at most six words>"
Music: <one sentence — genre, mood, tempo and instruments of the instrumental soundtrack>
Use only facts from the brief; never invent claims or specifications. No other headings, no commentary.
